Project Python Foundations: FoodHub Data Analysis¶

Marks: 60

Context¶

The number of restaurants in New York is increasing day by day. Lots of students and busy professionals rely on those restaurants due to their hectic lifestyles. Online food delivery service is a great option for them. It provides them with good food from their favorite restaurants. A food aggregator company FoodHub offers access to multiple restaurants through a single smartphone app.

The app allows the restaurants to receive a direct online order from a customer. The app assigns a delivery person from the company to pick up the order after it is confirmed by the restaurant. The delivery person then uses the map to reach the restaurant and waits for the food package. Once the food package is handed over to the delivery person, he/she confirms the pick-up in the app and travels to the customer's location to deliver the food. The delivery person confirms the drop-off in the app after delivering the food package to the customer. The customer can rate the order in the app. The food aggregator earns money by collecting a fixed margin of the delivery order from the restaurants.

Objective¶

The food aggregator company has stored the data of the different orders made by the registered customers in their online portal. They want to analyze the data to get a fair idea about the demand of different restaurants which will help them in enhancing their customer experience. Suppose you are hired as a Data Scientist in this company and the Data Science team has shared some of the key questions that need to be answered. Perform the data analysis to find answers to these questions that will help the company to improve the business.

Data Description¶

The data contains the different data related to a food order. The detailed data dictionary is given below.

Data Dictionary¶

  • order_id: Unique ID of the order
  • customer_id: ID of the customer who ordered the food
  • restaurant_name: Name of the restaurant
  • cuisine_type: Cuisine ordered by the customer
  • cost: Cost of the order
  • day_of_the_week: Indicates whether the order is placed on a weekday or weekend (The weekday is from Monday to Friday and the weekend is Saturday and Sunday)
  • rating: Rating given by the customer out of 5
  • food_preparation_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the restaurant to prepare the food. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the restaurant's order confirmation and the delivery person's pick-up confirmation.
  • delivery_time: Time (in minutes) taken by the delivery person to deliver the food package. This is calculated by taking the difference between the timestamps of the delivery person's pick-up confirmation and drop-off information

# Define the input and output file paths
input_file = 'foodhub_order.csv'
output_file = 'foodhub_order_cleaned.csv'

# Open the input CSV file for reading
with open(input_file, 'r') as infile:
    # Open the output CSV file for writing
    with open(output_file, 'w') as outfile:
        # Iterate through each line in the input file
        for line in infile:
            # Split the line into columns
            columns = line.strip().split(',')
            # Check if the 'rating' column is not "Not Given"
            if columns[6] != 'Not Given':
                # Write the line to the output file
                outfile.write(line)

# Load the cleaned data from the output CSV file into a DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(output_file)

Question 8: Which is the most popular cuisine on weekends? [1 mark]¶

In [26]:
# Convert 'day_of_the_week' column to lowercase for case-insensitive comparison
df['day_of_the_week'] = df['day_of_the_week'].str.lower()

# Filter the data to include only orders placed on weekends (Saturday or Sunday)
weekend_orders = df[(df['day_of_the_week'] == 'saturday') | (df['day_of_the_week'] == 'sunday')]

# Group the filtered data by cuisine type and count the number of orders for each cuisine type
cuisine_orders = weekend_orders.groupby('cuisine_type')['order_id'].count()

# Check if cuisine_orders is not empty
if not cuisine_orders.empty:
    # Get the cuisine type(s) with the highest number of orders
    most_popular_cuisines = cuisine_orders[cuisine_orders == cuisine_orders.max()]

    # Display the most popular cuisine(s) on weekends
    print("The most popular cuisine(s) on weekends is/are:", most_popular_cuisines.index.tolist())
else:
    print("No orders placed on weekends.")

Question 12: Perform a multivariate analysis to explore relationships between the important variables in the dataset. (It is a good idea to explore relations between numerical variables as well as relations between numerical and categorical variables) [10 marks]

In [15]:
# Load the data from CSV file
df = pd.read_csv('foodhub_order.csv')

# Select relevant columns for analysis
selected_columns = ['restaurant_name', 'cuisine_type', 'cost_of_the_order', 'day_of_the_week', 'rating', 'food_preparation_time', 'delivery_time']
df_selected = df[selected_columns].copy()  # Make a copy of the DataFrame to avoid modifying the original DataFrame

# Convert categorical variables to numerical using label encoding
label_encoder = LabelEncoder()
df_selected['cuisine_type_encoded'] = label_encoder.fit_transform(df_selected['cuisine_type'])
df_selected['day_of_the_week_encoded'] = label_encoder.fit_transform(df_selected['day_of_the_week'])

# Replace 'Not given' in 'rating' column with NaN
df_selected.loc[df_selected['rating'] == 'Not given', 'rating'] = pd.NA

# Drop non-numeric columns
numeric_columns = ['cost_of_the_order', 'rating', 'food_preparation_time', 'delivery_time']
df_numeric = df_selected[numeric_columns].copy()  # Make a copy of the DataFrame to avoid modifying the original DataFrame

# Convert 'rating' column to float
df_numeric['rating'] = pd.to_numeric(df_numeric['rating'], errors='coerce')

# Calculate the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = df_numeric.corr()

# Create a heatmap of the correlation matrix
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))
sns.heatmap(correlation_matrix, annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', fmt=".2f", linewidths=0.5)
plt.title('Correlation Heatmap')
plt.show()

Question 13: The company wants to provide a promotional offer in the advertisement of the restaurants. The condition to get the offer is that the restaurants must have a rating count of more than 50 and the average rating should be greater than 4. Find the restaurants fulfilling the criteria to get the promotional offer. [3 marks]¶

Observations:¶

The analysis reveals several restaurants eligible for the promotional offer, including Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken, Blue Ribbon Sushi, Shake Shack, and The Meatball Shop. These establishments exhibit noteworthy average ratings and substantial rating counts, indicating high customer satisfaction and engagement. They also maintain consistently high ratings, making them strong candidates for promotional offers to attract more customers and boost business.

Question 14: The company charges the restaurant 25% on the orders having cost greater than 20 dollars and 15% on the orders having cost greater than 5 dollars. Find the net revenue generated by the company across all orders. [3 marks]¶

In [6]:
# Assuming you've already read the CSV file into a DataFrame named 'df'

# Calculate the revenue generated by each order
df['revenue'] = df['cost_of_the_order']

# Determine the charges applicable to each order based on the specified criteria
df['charges'] = 0  # Initialize charges column
df.loc[df['cost_of_the_order'] > 20, 'charges'] = df['cost_of_the_order'] * 0.25  # 25% charge for orders > $20
df.loc[(df['cost_of_the_order'] <= 20) & (df['cost_of_the_order'] > 5), 'charges'] = df['cost_of_the_order'] * 0.15  # 15% charge for orders > $5 and <= $20

# Calculate the net revenue
total_revenue = df['revenue'].sum()
total_charges = df['charges'].sum()
net_revenue = total_revenue - total_charges

# Display the net revenue
print("Net revenue generated by the company across all orders: $", round(net_revenue, 2))

Net revenue generated by the company across all orders: $ 15610.44

Observations:¶

The company has earned a total of $15610.44 from all the orders placed. This shows that the company has made a good amount of money from its customers, indicating that its business is doing well financially.

Question 15: The company wants to analyze the total time required to deliver the food. What percentage of orders take more than 60 minutes to get delivered from the time the order is placed? (The food has to be prepared and then delivered.) [2 marks]¶

In [7]:
# Calculate the total time required for each order to be delivered
df['total_delivery_time'] = df['food_preparation_time'] + df['delivery_time']

# Determine the percentage of orders that exceed 60 minutes in delivery time
orders_exceeding_60_minutes = df[df['total_delivery_time'] > 60]
percentage_orders_exceeding_60_minutes = (len(orders_exceeding_60_minutes) / len(df)) * 100

# Display the percentage of orders that exceed 60 minutes in delivery time
print("Percentage of orders that take more than 60 minutes to get delivered:", round(percentage_orders_exceeding_60_minutes, 2), "%")

Percentage of orders that take more than 60 minutes to get delivered: 10.24 %

Approximately 10.24% of the orders take more than 60 minutes to be delivered. This suggests that a notable portion of the orders experiences longer delivery times, which could potentially affect customer satisfaction and retention. The company may need to focus on optimizing delivery processes to reduce wait times and enhance overall service quality.

Mean Delivery Time on Weekdays: 28.305882352941175
Mean Delivery Time on Weekends: 22.436739659367397

Observations:¶

On weekdays, the average delivery time is around 28.3 minutes, while on weekends, it's approximately 22.4 minutes. This indicates that deliveries tend to be faster on weekends compared to weekdays. Customers may receive their orders quicker on weekends, possibly because there's less traffic or fewer orders being placed, making it easier for delivery personnel to navigate and fulfill orders promptly.

Conclusion and Recommendations¶

Question 17: What are your conclusions from the analysis? What recommendations would you like to share to help improve the business? (You can use cuisine type and feedback ratings to drive your business recommendations.) [6 marks]¶

Conclusions:¶

  • Delivery Efficiency: Analysis revealed that delivery times are generally shorter on weekends compared to weekdays, suggesting the need for optimized logistics and staffing during peak hours to maintain consistent service quality.

  • Customer Feedback: A considerable number of orders remain unrated, indicating a potential gap in the feedback collection process. Encouraging customers to rate their orders could provide valuable insights into service quality and areas for improvement.

  • Promotional Opportunities: Identifying restaurants with high ratings and sufficient rating counts presents an opportunity for targeted promotional offers. This strategy can help incentivize customers to patronize well-rated establishments, thereby boosting overall customer satisfaction and loyalty.

  • Revenue Generation: The company's net revenue from orders is $15,610.44, reflecting the financial performance of the business over the analyzed period.

Recommendations:¶

  • Enhanced Feedback Mechanism: Implement a proactive feedback system to encourage customers to rate their orders, possibly through post-order notifications or incentives like discount codes for completing feedback forms. This will help gather more comprehensive insights into customer satisfaction and preferences.

  • Logistics Optimization: Invest in route optimization software and real-time tracking tools to streamline delivery operations, particularly during peak hours. Efficient logistics can lead to shorter delivery times, enhancing customer satisfaction and retention.

  • Promotional Campaigns: Launch targeted promotional campaigns for restaurants with high ratings and significant rating counts. Offer exclusive discounts or loyalty rewards to incentivize customers to patronize these establishments, thereby driving traffic and revenue.

  • Diversified Cuisine Offerings: Analyze customer preferences based on cuisine types and introduce a diverse range of offerings to cater to varied tastes. Collaborate with popular restaurants to expand the menu and attract a wider customer base, thereby increasing order volume and revenue.
